transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it’s really nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... my sleep has just gotten a little, well, messed up lately. I hope it's okay to come in for something like that. 

It's probably just normal stress or something, but... I'll either stay up half the night because my mind is just sort of running, or I'll wake up way too early and feel like I never really rested at all. I mean, I'm still getting all my bookkeeping work done and everything, I promise, it's just getting a little frustrating. Does that make sense? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out, if that's all right.
When this happens, do you feel like you need less sleep than usual?

Um, yeah, actually... I hope it doesn't sound too weird, but yes. There were several nights recently where I only managed to get maybe three or four hours of sleep. But the funny thing is, I didn't feel exhausted or anything, which I guess is a good thing, right? 

I actually got up feeling really... charged. Like, I didn't even need my usual coffee to get going for the day. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm doing it on purpose or being irresponsible with my schedule, it just sort of happens. But I felt completely fine on that little sleep. Is that... is that something you see a lot? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right, if that makes sense.
During those days after only a few hours of sleep, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Um, well... I wouldn't necessarily say euphoric. That sounds a little extreme, you know? But... I guess earlier in the month, I did feel really good. Like, almost lit up and unstoppable, if that makes sense? I was getting so much done. I hope that's okay to say, I mean, it felt like a positive thing at first.

But, um... then I started getting a little... well, I don't want to sound like a difficult person, because I really try to be easy to work with. But I noticed I'd snap at my mom, or even my supervisor at work, over just little questions. Things that normally wouldn't bother me at all. I felt so bad about it afterward. I'm usually very patient, I promise. Do you think... do you think feeling that good at first could be connected to getting so irritable later? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
During that time, did you find yourself taking on a lot more activities or projects than usual?

Um, yeah, I guess I did. I mean, I was just feeling so productive, which is usually a good trait, right? I didn't want to waste that energy. 

I started... well, I was emailing a bunch of people to see if they needed help with their books, just trying to be helpful. And I started mapping out all these ideas for fixing up my condo, which I've been meaning to do anyway. I even called a few relatives to talk through some of the plans. I was just really motivated. I hope it doesn't sound like I was being too intense or bothering anyone... I just wanted to make the most of feeling so capable. Is it normal to get a little carried away when you're feeling that good?
About how many days in a row did that period of feeling unusually energized and needing very little sleep last?

Um, let me think... I want to make sure I give you the right timeline. I think it was maybe... a few days? Like, maybe four or five days in a row where I felt like that? 

I hope that doesn't sound like too long to be acting like that. I really did try to settle down and get back to my normal routine, I promise. It just sort of stretched out for a little bit before I crashed. Does four or five days sound about right for what you usually hear from people? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
During that period, did your mood or energy cause serious problems at work, at home, or with other people?

Um, well... I wouldn't say *serious* problems. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or not doing my job, because I really am trying my best. I'm still getting to work every day, I promise. 

But, um... I guess I have made a few little mistakes lately. Just some reconciliation errors with the accounts. My supervisor did pull me aside to talk about it, which was... well, it was really embarrassing. I felt terrible, because I always want to do good work for them. 

And, um, outside of work... I've sort of been skipping my salsa class. And I haven't really been seeing my friends as much. I just... I don't quite feel like myself right now, and I don't want to bring anyone down or be a burden, you know? I hope that makes sense. Is it okay that I've been pulling back a little bit just to try and get myself sorted out?
After that energized period ended, did you go through a stretch where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um, yeah... I guess so. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or being ungrateful, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But, um... yeah, after that energy wore off, I just... I sort of crashed. 

Lately, I've been waking up with this really heavy, empty feeling. It's hard to explain, but it's like... even just sitting in my condo, which I worked so hard to get and fix up, it just makes me want to cry. I try really hard to shake it off, I promise, because I know I need to keep it together for work and everything. But it's just been lingering most of the day. Is it normal to feel that down after having a few really good days? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
At its longest, did that unusually energized period last at least 7 days?

Um, no, definitely not that long. I wouldn't want you to think it was a whole week of me being like that. I really do try to keep a handle on things. Like I said, it was just maybe four or five days tops before I kind of ran out of steam. I hope that's okay? I just want to be really clear that it wasn't a full week or anything too crazy.
During this low period, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Um, well... I guess I have, a little bit. I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or like I'm giving up on things, because I'm not, I promise. 

It's just... like I mentioned before, I stopped going to my salsa class. I usually love it, but lately it just feels like too much effort. And, um, I also like to paint in my free time. But my paints have just been sitting out on the table for a while now. I look at them and I just... I feel nothing. It's almost like they belong to somebody else. 

I know I should be doing my hobbies to stay active, and I feel really guilty for just letting them sit there. Is it okay that I'm taking a little break from those things right now? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get better.
Have you been feeling down like this for at least two weeks?

Um... yeah, it's... it's definitely been longer than two weeks. I'm almost embarrassed to admit this, because I really try not to be a complainer, but... it's actually been about five months. 

It's just been this sort of... depressed, guilty fog hanging around for all that time. I mean, I've still been going to my bookkeeping job every day and trying my best to push through it, I promise! I really thought I could just snap myself out of it if I worked hard enough. But it just got so much worse recently, right after I bought the condo. 

I hope it's okay that I waited this long to come see you? I just didn't want to bother anyone or seem weak, but I want to do whatever I'm supposed to do to get back on track.
